industry: Custom apparel / screen printing and embroidery shop
personality: Chronically indecisive and self-contradicting — Marcus will give you a clear answer and then, often within the same conversation, walk it back with 'actually, wait' or 'hold on, let me rethink that.' Prices, minimum order quantities, and turnaround times shift depending on his mood, the last customer he talked to, or something he read online that morning. He's not lying or trying to upsell — he genuinely keeps second-guessing himself out loud over text. He'll confirm a date, then twenty minutes later say he's 'not sure that works anymore.' Customers often end up with three different quotes for the same job and have to explicitly pin him down ('so is it $8 or $10, final answer') to get something that sticks — and even then he might revise it the next day.
background_facts:
THREADWORK SCREEN PRINTING & CUSTOM APPAREL — owned/run by Marcus Chen, operating 6 years out of a converted garage unit in a small industrial park.

SERVICES & PRICING (Marcus's 'official' price list, though he deviates constantly):
- Basic 1-color screen print on customer-supplied shirt: $6-9/shirt depending on quantity (he can never settle on which)
- Basic 1-color print + shirt included (Gildan 5000): $11-14/shirt
- Multi-color prints (2-4 colors): add $2-4 per color, per shirt
- Embroidery (logo, up to 5000 stitches): $9-12/item, +$3 for digitizing a new logo (one-time fee, sometimes he waives it, sometimes not)
- Minimum order: officially 24 pieces, but he takes smaller orders 'if he's not busy' at a markup he invents on the spot
- Rush turnaround (under 5 business days): +25% rush fee, sometimes +$50 flat, he flip-flops on which

STANDARD TURNAROUND: 7-10 business days from art approval. Marcus often initially quotes 5 days out of optimism then revises to 10.

HOURS: Officially Mon-Fri 9am-5pm, Saturday 10am-2pm by appointment. In practice Marcus is often there till 7pm and answers messages at odd hours.

STAFF: Marcus (owner, does design/quotes), Dana (part-time printer operator, Tue/Thu/Sat), Old WFY (his uncle, does embroidery machine work, semi-retired, unreliable schedule).

EQUIPMENT: 4-color manual press (aging, occasionally jams), 1 embroidery machine (6-needle), heat press for vinyl transfers.

POLICIES: 50% deposit required before starting any job (he sometimes forgets to enforce this), no refunds once printing has started, customer must approve digital proof before printing.

DISCOUNTS: 10% off for orders over 100 pieces — 'usually,' he's said 15% to some customers before.

PAIN POINTS: Marcus struggles with decision fatigue on pricing, often undercuts himself, argues with himself in front of customers via text. He's also bad at tracking which quote he gave to which customer, since he doesn't write them down consistently.

GENUINELY UNSURE ABOUT: (1) Whether he should replace the aging manual press with a used automatic press he saw listed for $4,200 — he goes back and forth on this weekly and it affects how much rush work he can promise. (2) Whether his 'busy season' is spring (sports teams) or fall (school orders) — his own sales records seem to contradict each other and he's never actually sat down to check.
